user.title: What should it learn from?
user.description: Pick one or more entities that show when something is in use: a power sensor, the device itself, a media player, a motion sensor … There is nothing else to set up; what counts as active is learned from the data.

control.title: What should be controlled?
control.description: Pick the entity that should be switched on and off for you.

error.no_entities: Pick at least one entity to learn from.

abort.already_configured: This entity is already controlled by a pattern.

data.guard_grace_minutes: Switch off after being unused for

data_description.learn_entities: The controlled entity counts as in use while any of these is active. For numeric sensors, what counts as active is worked out from the data.
data_description.lead_minutes: Minutes before the learned start of use.
data_description.off_delay_minutes: Minutes after the learned end of use.
data_description.guard_grace_minutes: The entity is never switched off while in use. Once it has been unused for this long, a postponed switch-off happens.
data_description.window_days: Older data is forgotten and recent days count more, so the model follows slow changes on its own.
data_description.min_days: Nothing is predicted before this many complete days were observed. It is also how many days are needed to tell weekdays apart.
data_description.min_confidence: A period counts as a habit when the model is at least this sure there is use.
